hook: Antoine Bordes earned a PhD in artificial intelligence from Sorbonne University in Paris in 2010, work recognized with best doctoral research awards from the French Association for Artificial Intelligence and the French Armament Agency. He then held a postdoctoral position in Yoshua Bengio's lab at the University of Montreal and worked as a research scientist at CNRS in France. In 2013 he co-authored Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data, introducing TransE, a simple and influential method for embedding entities and relations from knowledge graphs into a shared vector space. He joined Facebook, later Meta, in 2014 and spent nine years building the Fundamental AI Research lab, serving as its global co-managing director for the final three years of his tenure. In March 2023 he left Meta to become Vice President of Artificial Intelligence at Helsing, a European defense technology company, where he leads AI research and engineering.

standing.record: The site's records tie Bordes to two companies, Helsing and Meta, and to a set of lawsuits that name Meta rather than him. Neural AI, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc., summary judgment was granted for Meta on fair use in June 2025, and plaintiffs seek interlocutory appeal certification as of 2026-08-25. In State of New Mexico ex rel. Torrez v. Meta Platforms, Inc., a jury verdict for the state on September 25, 2026 found Facebook liable for deceiving users about privacy protections, with more than 43 million violations of the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act, and penalties are to be set at a hearing on October 1, 2026, with the state seeking up to $5,000 per violation, while claims that Facebook misrepresented removal of harmful content were rejected. The pattern in these records is a research and executive career at Meta and Helsing, with legal exposure attached to Meta and not to Bordes or Helsing.
standing.standing: Antoine Bordes stands as Vice President of Artificial Intelligence at Helsing, a European defense technology company, where he leads AI research and engineering, according to the records. He is listed as an executive of Helsing and of Meta. His background includes a 2010 PhD in artificial intelligence from Sorbonne University in Paris, a postdoctoral position in Yoshua Bengio's lab at the University of Montreal, and work as a research scientist at CNRS. He co-authored the 2013 TransE paper, Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data, and is described as a pioneer of knowledge graph embeddings. He spent nine years at Facebook and Meta, including three years as global co-managing director of Meta's Fundamental AI Research lab, and has published more than 60 papers with tens of thousands of citations.
